traceability.evidence: Story file present and in-scope: docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md (content matches the provided specification).,New ESLint rule implemented for this story: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts. - Rule JSDoc explicitly ties it to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS`, `REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY`, `REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX`, `REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID`, `REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT`, `REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT`, `REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE`, `REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT`. - Options defined per story: `testFilePatterns`, `requireDescribeStory`, `requireTestReqPrefix`, `describePattern`, `autoFixTestTemplate`, `autoFixTestPrefixFormat`, `testSupportsTemplate`. - meta.messages match the story’s error message examples exactly: - `missingFileSupports`: "Test file must have @supports annotation listing tested requirements." - `missingDescribeStory`: "describe() block should reference story (e.g., 'Story 009.0-DEV-...')." - `missingReqPrefix`: "Test name should start with requirement ID (e.g., '[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] ...').",Helper module implements core behavior: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts. - Test file detection (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT): `determineIsTestFile` uses default patterns `["/tests/", "/test/", "/__tests__", ".test.", ".spec."]` and configurable `testFilePatterns` to detect test files by path substring (matches story’s Test File Detection notes). - File-level @supports enforcement (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID): `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` scans all comments with `/@supports\b/` and, if missing, reports `messageId: "missingFileSupports"` and optionally inserts a safe placeholder `@supports` JSDoc template via `insertSupportsTemplate` and `buildSupportsTemplateComment`. This ensures test files have a file-level `@supports` annotation. - Framework compatibility (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT): `isTestCallName` returns true for `"describe"`, `"it"`, `"test"`, `"context"`, covering Jest-style and Mocha-style test APIs. - Describe block story reference validation (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT): `handleCallExpression` builds a `CallExpression` visitor which: - Computes `calleeName` (supports `describe`, `it`, `test`, `context`, including member calls where the object is an Identifier). - For `describe`, calls `handleDescribeCall` which checks description string against configurable `describeRegex` (default `"Story [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+-"`) and reports `messageId: "missingDescribeStory"` when it doesn’t match. This applies to all matching describe calls in test files (top-level and nested). - Test name requirement prefixes (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT): `handleItOrTestCall` enforces that `it`/`test` descriptions start with `/^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/` when `requireTestReqPrefix` is true, otherwise reports `messageId: "missingReqPrefix"`. - Auto-fix for malformed prefixes (linked story 021.0, but used here): `normalizeReqId`, `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription`, and `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw` safely normalize malformed prefixes like `[ REQ-XXX ]`, `[REQ_XXX]`, `[req-xxx]`, `(REQ-XXX)` without inventing new IDs (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE).,Rule wiring and integration with plugin infrastructure (AC: Integration, Quality Standards): - src/index.ts includes the rule in the dynamic rule registry: - `const RULE_NAMES = [ ..., "require-test-traceability", ] as const;` - Dynamic loader `require(./rules/${name})` ensures the rule is discoverable like all others. - The rule is mapped into severity presets (Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING): - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` includes `"traceability/require-test-traceability": "error"`. - Both `recommended` and `strict` configs include this rule via `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()` (verified by tests below and by the user docs).,Unit tests specifically for this story and its auto-fix companion story: tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts. - File header: - `@supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT` - `@supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md ...` for the auto-fix story. - Valid cases: - REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS: test with file-level @supports and proper describe and it name: - Code: `/** @supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS */ describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', () => { it('[REQ-EXAMPLE] does something', () => {}); });` - Confirms file-level @supports, describe story reference, and `[REQ-XXX]` prefix all satisfy the rule. - REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT: Mocha-style `context(...)` is treated as a test call (name checks apply) for filename `tests/some/context.test.ts`. - REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT: `src/not-a-test-file.ts` is ignored despite containing describe/it, validating that non-test files are not subject to this rule. - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT: already-correct `[REQ-TRACE-123]` prefix is left unchanged by auto-fix. - Invalid cases: - REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE & REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS: missing file-level @supports in a test file triggers `messageId: "missingFileSupports"` and auto-inserts placeholder template at the top, matching the story’s example template (safe and non-semantic, with TODO guidance). - REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY: a describe without story phrase (`'no story reference here'`) yields an error `messageId: "missingDescribeStory"`. - REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX & REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE: `it('missing prefix', ...)` triggers `missingReqPrefix`, with no auto-fix because there is no recognizable REQ id to normalize. - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT: malformed prefixes are normalized via auto-fix: - `'[ REQ-TEST-FIX ] does something'` → `'[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'`. - `'[REQ_TEST_FIX] does something'` → `'[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'`. - `'[req-lowercase] bad casing'` → `'[REQ-LOWERCASE] bad casing'`. - `'(REQ-PAREN) with parens'` → `'[REQ-PAREN] with parens'`.,Test run confirms the rule’s test suite passes (from `npm test -- --verbose`): - The same doc lists this rule as enabled at `error` severity in both the `recommended` and `strict` presets, satisfying the story’s documentation and integration expectations. user-docs/examples.md references the rule to align examples with its expectations.,Requirements from the story mapped to implementation: - REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS: Implemented and tested via `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` and corresponding valid/invalid test cases. - REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY: Implemented via `handleDescribeCall` with configurable `describePattern`, tested with a bad describe string producing `missingDescribeStory`. - REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX: Implemented via `handleItOrTestCall` and enforced regex prefix check; numerous tests cover both compliant and non-compliant names. - REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID: File-level @supports presence and shape is enforced here; deeper validation that story paths and requirement IDs are real is handled by existing rules from dependency stories (valid-story-reference and valid-req-reference) which apply to all code, including tests. Together, they ensure test-file `@supports` annotations are both present and refer to valid stories/requirements. - REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT: `determineIsTestFile` and `testFilePatterns` option implement this; traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION are implemented and verified. The `traceability/require-test-traceability` rule enforces file-level @supports annotations, describe-block story references, and [REQ-XXX] prefixes for test names, with configurable behavior and safe auto-fixes. It is integrated into the plugin’s rule registry and presets, documented in user-facing docs, and fully covered by passing unit tests, including tests that explicitly reference this story and its requirements. The deeper validity of @supports references is handled by existing validation rules from the declared dependency stories, which apply equally to test files.
